title: Hostile Inference: Exploiting Docker Model Runner for Container Escapes
content_md: Local LLM inference is seeing adoption in default developer workflows, and the tooling that serves those models now ships inside products developers already trust. One of those is Docker Model Runner (DMR), the feature in Docker Desktop that pulls, runs, and serves models locally. In November 2025, we reported ZDI-26-150 / CVE-2026-28400 , a denial-of-service (on macOS) stemming from an unauthenticated argument-injection vulnerability in DMR. A container created with the default set of privileges could overwrite and corrupt the Docker Desktop VM’s data disk. Further analysis, under non-default configurations, turned the same primitive into arbitrary code execution on the host, on both macOS and Windows. In this post, we walk through the full chain: the argument-injection primitive, the host file read/write foothold it grants, how we take partial control of what gets written, and the payoff that turns a constrained file write into arbitrary code execution on the host through Docker Extensions. We then cover two further escapes we found along the way: one from an overly permissive Seatbelt sandbox configuration on macOS, and one that pivots the WSL2 VM-to-host boundary through Docker Extensions. Background: Docker Model Runner and the host boundary Docker Desktop helps run Docker containers on macOS, Windows, and Linux.
